questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: A peer claims BGP selects the path with the fewest hops. Your correction:
options: BGP is policy-driven; the decision process uses attributes such as Weight, Local Preference, AS-path length, Origin, MED, then IGP cost—not raw hop count
BGP ignores all attributes except MED
questions.explanation: Doyle Vol II: BGP decision process literacy beats 'shortest path' folklore.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Why do large ASes need route reflectors or confederations for iBGP?
options: Full-mesh iBGP does not re-advertise iBGP-learned routes, so scale needs RR/confeds (or add-path designs) to distribute paths without an N² mesh
OSPF forbids more than two BGP speakers
questions.explanation: iBGP split-horizon drives RR/confederation architecture.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: In a Clos fabric built per RFC 7938, why is eBGP often preferred as the underlay routing protocol?
options: eBGP gives clear AS boundaries, simple policy knobs, and scales with ECMP without flooding a full IGP topology into every leaf
eBGP only works over the public Internet
questions.explanation: Modern DC: eBGP Clos underlay pattern.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Local Preference vs AS-path for outbound path selection inside one AS:
options: Local Preference is local to the AS and preferred earlier in the decision process; AS-path length compares after Local Pref (among other steps)
questions.explanation: Order of BGP decision process matters for ops.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: When is MED most useful?
options: Influencing which entry point a neighboring AS prefers into your AS when multiple links exist—MED is typically compared between paths from the same neighboring AS
questions.explanation: MED is an inter-AS ingress preference signal with caveats.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: A team wants operators to tag routes for later filtering without changing AS-path. Best tool:
options: BGP communities (or large/extended communities) as opaque tags for policy
questions.explanation: Communities are the workhorse for scalable BGP policy.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: BGP session stuck in Active/Connect—most likely class of issue?
options: TCP session / reachability / ACL / wrong peer IP or ASN—not a finished OPEN exchange
questions.explanation: FSM literacy: Idle/Connect/Active/OpenSent/OpenConfirm/Established.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: iBGP advertises a prefix but the next-hop is unreachable. Symptom:
options: Route may be in RIB as invalid/hidden until next-hop is resolvable via IGP/static—or next-hop-self is applied on the edge
questions.explanation: Next-hop reachability is a classic Dive Deep trap.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Update-group / peer-group style scaling helps because:
options: Speakers can format and replicate updates efficiently across peers that share the same outbound policy
They remove the need for TCP
questions.explanation: Control-plane CPU and formatting cost at scale.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Graceful Restart / long-lived graceful restart aims to:
options: Preserve forwarding during control-plane restart so data plane can keep forwarding while sessions re-establish
questions.explanation: Separate control plane restart from forwarding continuity.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Why does OSPF use areas?
options: To bound LSDB size and SPF blast radius—ABRs summarize/filter between areas while Area 0 is the backbone
questions.explanation: Doyle Vol I: hierarchical OSPF design.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Type 1 vs Type 2 LSA roles:
options: Type 1 (Router) describes a router's links; Type 2 (Network) describes a multi-access network and attached routers (DR-originated)
questions.explanation: LSA type literacy for adjacency/topology debugging.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Type 3 vs Type 5 LSA:
options: Type 3 (Summary) is ABR-originated inter-area; Type 5 (External) is ASBR-originated redistributed external routes (Type 4 finds the ASBR)
questions.explanation: External vs summary is a frequent exam/interview discriminator.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Two OSPF routers on a LAN form 2-Way but not Full. Likely focus:
options: DR/BDR election and adjacency only to DR/BDR on broadcast—or MTU/area/network-type/hello mismatch blocking FULL
questions.explanation: Neighbor state machine: Down→Init→2-Way→ExStart→Exchange→Loading→Full.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: An engineer proposes running OSPF as a single area across a huge DC. Risk:
options: LSDB and SPF scale poorly—churn floods everywhere; hierarchy or alternate design (e.g. eBGP Clos) is usually safer
questions.explanation: Capacity of the control plane is a manager concern.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Stub / totally stubby / NSSA intent:
options: Reduce external (and optionally summary) LSAs in an area, injecting a default instead—NSSA allows limited external origination
questions.explanation: Area types trade reachability detail for scale.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: OSPF path selection basics:
options: Intra-area paths preferred over inter-area; lowest cost wins; equal-cost paths can ECMP
Local Pref is an OSPF LSA
questions.explanation: Contrast with BGP policy model.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Redistributing BGP into OSPF without filters—manager concern:
options: Control-plane and LSDB explosion; suboptimal paths; feedback loops—need careful filtering, tags, and metrics
OSPF automatically aggregates Internet table safely
questions.explanation: Mutual redistribution is a classic blast-radius topic.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Point-to-point vs broadcast OSPF network types matter because:
options: They change adjacency model (DR or not), timers expectations, and how links appear in the LSDB
They change TCP window size only
questions.explanation: Mismatched network types → stubborn adjacency issues.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: OSPFv2 vs OSPFv3 high-level difference:
options: OSPFv3 is redesigned for IPv6 (and can carry IPv4 with extensions); addressing/flooding details differ from OSPFv2's IPv4-centric design
OSPFv3 removes the concept of areas
questions.explanation: Know they are related but not drop-in identical.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: IS-IS Level-1 vs Level-2:
options: L1 is intra-area routing; L2 is backbone/inter-area; L1-L2 routers attach areas to the L2 backbone (mental model analogous to OSPF areas)
questions.explanation: Doyle Vol I IS-IS hierarchy.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Why is IS-IS often described as TLV-extensible?
options: Protocol data uses Type-Length-Value encoding, easing new address families and capabilities without redesigning the core
questions.explanation: Extensibility is a key IS-IS selling point historically.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Practical reason some operators prefer IS-IS over OSPF in SP/DC cores:
options: Runs over L2 (not IP), historically strong multi-AF/TLV story and operational familiarity—tradeoffs, not universal superiority
questions.explanation: Interview answer: tradeoffs + ops culture, not dogma.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: An IS-IS NET address encodes:
options: Area and system ID (NSAP/NET format)—misconfigured area/system ID prevents adjacency
questions.explanation: Addressing mistakes are common IS-IS breaks.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Wide metrics in IS-IS matter because:
options: Narrow metrics are too coarse for modern TE/ECMP designs; wide metrics give finer cost control
questions.explanation: Cost granularity for traffic engineering style ops.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Setting the IS-IS overload bit is used to:
options: Signal that the node should be avoided for transit during maintenance/boot until ready
questions.explanation: Maintenance hygiene analogous to max-metric tricks.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: IS-IS adjacency fails—checklist includes:
options: Level mismatch, NET/area mismatch, MTU, authentication, circuit type, and whether both sides expect point-to-point vs broadcast
Only Security Group rules in AWS
questions.explanation: Same debugging discipline as OSPF, different knobs.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: L1 router installs a default toward L1-L2 because:
options: Attached bit / default origination from L1-L2 provides inter-area exit without full L2 topology in L1
BGP RR reflects defaults into IS-IS automatically
questions.explanation: Hierarchy leak of default, not full Internet.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: What does an MPLS label primarily do in the data plane?
options: Indexes a short label-switched forwarding decision (LFIB) so core LSRs can forward without IP lookup on every hop
questions.explanation: MPLS Fundamentals: label switching idea.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: A packet with a label stack arrives; the LSR typically:
options: Looks up the top label and may swap/push/pop per LFIB—PHP often pops the penultimate label
Always strips all labels and floods L2
questions.explanation: Push/swap/pop + penultimate hop popping concept.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: LDP's role:
options: Distribute label bindings for FECs so LSPs can be established for IGP-learned prefixes (common LDP+IGP model)
questions.explanation: Control plane for labels alongside IGP.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: RSVP-TE is used when you need:
options: Traffic-engineered LSPs with bandwidth/constraint routing—not just follow-IGP LDP paths
questions.explanation: TE vs vanilla shortest-path label distribution.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: In MPLS L3VPN, VRF + RD + RT divide labor as:
options: VRF separates tables; RD makes prefixes unique in BGP; RTs control which VPNs import/export which routes
RD encrypts packets; RT is a VLAN ID
RT is only for LDP hello
questions.explanation: Core L3VPN mental model for interviews.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: VPNv4 BGP carries:
options: Labeled VPN prefixes (RD:prefix) so PEs can exchange customer routes across a shared MPLS core
questions.explanation: MP-BGP as VPN control plane.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: P vs PE router roles:
options: PE (Provider Edge) maintains VRFs/customer adjacency; P (Provider) typically switches labels in the core without customer routes
P routers store all Internet + VPN tables
P routers terminate customer CE sessions
questions.explanation: Separation keeps core scalable.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Penultimate hop popping (PHP) exists to:
options: Let the egress PE avoid an unnecessary label lookup by receiving an IP (or inner) packet from the penultimate LSR
questions.explanation: Classic MPLS optimization detail.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: BFD paired with BGP/OSPF/IS-IS helps because:
options: Sub-second forwarding-plane liveliness detection can trigger faster session teardown than hello timers alone
questions.explanation: Fast failure detection cross-cutting control planes.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: ECMP in the FIB means:
options: Multiple equal-cost next hops installed; hashing spreads flows—watch polarization and unequal member health
One next hop always wins randomly per packet with no hash
questions.explanation: Underlay scale tool with operational caveats.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Segment Routing vs classic LDP—manager-level distinction:
options: SR encodes the path/segments in the packet (often MPLS or IPv6 SID) reducing per-flow state in the core versus distributed LDP bindings—EVPN is a separate overlay control plane for L2/L3 VPN services
SR deletes the need for an IGP
SR and EVPN are identical protocols
questions.explanation: Light awareness only—don't over-claim expertise.

questions.source: ANDM technical domains 2026-07 (Doyle / MPLS Fundamentals / RFC 7938)
questions.question: Mutually redistributing OSPF ↔ BGP without tags/filters—failure mode:
options: Route feedback loops, suboptimal paths, and control-plane overload—use tags, prefer points, and tight prefix filters
questions.explanation: Cross-protocol policy is where outages hide.
